title: What is Precedent Transaction analysis?
subtitle: Valuing a company based on prices actually paid in similar past M&A deals
openingQuestion: What is the core difference between Precedent Transaction Analysis and Comparable Company Analysis?
openingOptions: Precedent Transaction uses the ACTUAL prices paid in completed past M&A deals (including a control premium), while Comps uses ordinary trading prices on the exchange (no control premium)
There is no difference - the two methods are identical
Precedent Transaction only applies to unlisted companies
Comps always produces a higher result than Precedent Transaction
explanation: Precedent Transaction Analysis: study similar completed M&A deals (same industry, comparable size), take the valuation multiples that were actually paid (not everyday exchange trading prices) to estimate the target company's value. Because a buyer usually has to pay a 'control premium' to gain controlling ownership, Precedent Transaction multiples are typically HIGHER than Comps.

diagram.label: Find a similar completed M&A deal
Apply it to the current valuation

realWorldExample.description: When valuing a bank about to be acquired, analysts typically reference the P/B multiples actually paid in previous, similar bank M&A deals - usually significantly higher than the bank's ordinary trading P/B.

quiz.question: Why are Precedent Transaction multiples usually higher than Comparable Company Analysis multiples?
options: Because the buyer has to pay a control premium to gain control
Because Precedent Transaction is only used for large-cap companies
Because published M&A deal data is always inaccurate
There is no systematic difference between the two valuation methods
quiz.explanation: The control premium reflects the value of control itself: a controlling owner can change management, strategy and capital structure to optimise the company's value.

quiz.question: A precedent transaction happened during an extremely hot M&A market (multiple bidders competing for the same target). Should its multiple be applied directly to value a similar company today, in a quiet M&A market?
options: Precedent Transaction is never affected by market conditions, since it is fixed at signing
It needs adjusting - the multiple is highly sensitive to market conditions at the time
Being in the same industry is enough on its own, regardless of timing
Yes, apply it directly since both are deals in the same industry
quiz.explanation: This is an important limitation of Precedent Transaction Analysis: the multiple reflects M&A market conditions AT THE TIME the deal happened (competitive intensity, market sentiment).

quiz.question: Why are Precedent Transaction multiples usually higher than Comps?
options: Because M&A buyers usually skip thorough due diligence
Because M&A deals always happen when the market is at a high
Because the deal price already includes a premium for control
Because deal multiples are calculated on post-merger profit
quiz.explanation: Buying the right to decide always costs more than buying a minority stake. A 20-40% control premium sits inside every deal price, so applying that same multiple to a small stake overvalues it.

quiz.question: What is the problem with using a 2021 Precedent Transaction for a valuation today?
options: The parties in that deal may have since gone bankrupt
Old deal data is usually not fully disclosed
Accounting standards have changed, so the figures can't be compared
The multiple reflects market conditions from that specific point in time
quiz.explanation: Interest rates and risk appetite in 2021 were very different from today. A deal's multiple is a snapshot of one market at one moment, not an industry constant.

quiz.question: When is Precedent Transaction the most appropriate method to use?
options: When valuing a deal for acquiring control
When valuing a minority stake under five percent
When the business has no profit yet to calculate a multiple
When a quick number is needed with no market data available
quiz.explanation: Because the multiple already contains a control premium, it matches exactly the situation where the buyer is also acquiring control. Using it for any other purpose carries along a premium that doesn't belong to the buyer.

keyTakeaways: Precedent Transaction: uses actual prices from completed M&A deals
Usually includes a 'control premium', making the multiple higher than Comps
Useful when valuing a company in the context of a merger or full acquisition

practicePrompt.question: A PE fund is valuing a target company ahead of an acquisition, and references the prices other buyers actually paid when acquiring similar companies over the past 2-3 years (including the control premium). What is this valuation method called, and how does it differ from Comps?
options: Precedent Transaction uses prices from completed M&A deals, so it carries a control premium
This is actually the Comps method - there's no difference from comparing listed companies
This is the DCF method, since it estimates value from the company's historical data
This method is unreliable because it always relies on deals that are too old relative to today
practicePrompt.explanation: Precedent Transaction: uses actual prices from completed M&A deals. Unlike Comps (everyday stock trading prices, with no control rights), Precedent Transaction reflects the price actually paid to acquire full control of a company - so it is usually higher than Comps because it includes an acquisition premium.

summary.keyIdea: Precedent Transaction: uses actual prices from completed M&A deals
summary.commonMistake: Reading the concept as a definition to recite rather than a principle to apply to a real decision.
summary.action: Usually includes a 'control premium', making the multiple higher than Comps

application.title: Apply it now
application.message: The lesson already has a real example - the Masan-WinCommerce deal (valued at $2.8 billion USD) - see the 'Real example' section above. Now find another M&A deal yourself and estimate its multiple.
application.secondary: Recognising this premium helps you understand why M&A purchase prices are always higher than exchange trading prices.

sections.text: If you want to know what a company is truly worth when bought outright, don't look at everyday exchange trading prices - look at what buyers have actually paid in similar past M&A deals.

Precedent Transaction Analysis: study similar completed M&A deals (same industry, comparable size), take the valuation multiples actually paid to estimate the target company's value. When valuing a bank about to be acquired, analysts typically reference the P/B multiples paid in previous, similar bank M&A deals.
Why M&A multiples are usually higher than Comps

A buyer in an M&A deal usually has to pay a 'control premium' - an extra amount to gain control over and decision-making power at the target company. A controlling owner can change management, strategy and capital structure to optimise the company's value on their own terms - a right that doesn't exist for a small shareholder trading on the exchange. That is why M&A prices are usually higher than ordinary trading prices for the same company.

items: Precedent Transaction multiples are usually higher than Comps because they include a control premium
Highly sensitive to M&A market conditions at the time the deal happened
A deal from a hot M&A period (multiple competing bidders) should not be applied directly to a quiet period without adjustment
Most useful when valuing in the context of a merger or full acquisition, not a minority stock trade

sections.text: Real example: the Masan - WinCommerce deal

items: In 2024, SK Group (South Korea) sold a 7.1% stake in WinCommerce to Masan for $200 million USD - this price valued all of WinCommerce at roughly $2.8 billion USD
This is a real 'precedent transaction': valuing another retail chain in Vietnam could use the multiple (deal value / WinCommerce's revenue or EBITDA at that time) as a reference point
M&A multiples are usually higher than ordinary market valuation because the buyer pays an extra 'control premium' - the right to control the entire operation, not just a minority stake

sections.label: How to apply this yourself
sections.text: Find a recent M&A deal in the financial press (VnExpress, TheLEADER, Mekong ASEAN all cover M&A fairly thoroughly), determine the deal value, and estimate its multiple against the target company's most recently disclosed revenue/EBITDA.

lines: Precedent Transaction shows the actual price paid to take ownership - but always check the timing and market context of that deal.
